models.target: Complete umlaut feminine gāt paradigm and syncretism.

models.accepted_alternatives: The documented singular genitive gǣt and dative gāte are valid variants. The task’s selected paradigm uses gāte / gǣt.
models.diagnosis: Do not add -as to the nominative plural or extend the umlaut to gātum.

models.target: Selected instrumental forms, dative distinction and syncretism.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Masculine/neuter singular instrumental ðȳ (also ðon), strong adjective gōde; corresponding dative ðǣm, gōdum. Feminine singular and plural use dative-shaped forms for the instrumental relation.
models.accepted_alternatives: Both explicitly selected instrumental determiner variants are valid; a noun alone may not reveal whether its ending carries a dative or instrumental function.
models.diagnosis: Do not identify every -e as dative or replace the distinct instrumental adjective by dative gōdum in a task expressly asking for the distinct form.

models.target: Relational genitive versus a lexically governed genitive.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: The stranger’s son came. I ceased from the work. In the first, ðæs cuman is a genitive dependent of sunu; in the second, ðæs weorces is directly governed by geswāc.
models.accepted_alternatives: Stopped/ceased working conveys the second meaning, provided the analysis still identifies the genitive government.
models.diagnosis: A genitive is not necessarily a possessor, and its case does not depend on whether English uses of.

models.target: External dative head with an internal genitive dependent.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: The monk gave food to the stranger’s son. Suna is dative singular, the recipient; męte is accusative singular, the thing given; ðæs cuman is genitive singular, the stranger whose son is meant.
models.accepted_alternatives: Gave the stranger’s son food is equivalent.
models.diagnosis: Do not make cuman the direct recipient or let its genitive replace the head noun’s dative.

models.target: Agreeing attributive numeral versus substantival numeral with genitive whole.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: One monk came. One of the monks came. In the first ān agrees with nominative singular munuc; in the second ān stands as the nominative head and ðāra munuca is the genitive plural whole.
models.accepted_alternatives: A single monk came can express the first; the second must retain membership in the specified group.
models.diagnosis: The genitive plural does not make the head or finite verb plural.

models.target: Attributive cardinal count versus invariant fela with a genitive plural.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: I have two sheep. I have many sheep. Twā agrees with the neuter accusative plural scēap; invariant fela takes the genitive plural scēapa.
models.accepted_alternatives: A great many sheep is defensible for fela if the grammatical contrast is preserved.
models.diagnosis: Do not carry the agreeing cardinal’s accusative construction over to fela, and do not use masculine twēgen with sheep.

models.target: Dative recipient/person with accusative giving versus genitive denial.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: He gave food to the stranger. He denied the stranger food. The person is dative in both. Sęllan takes an accusative thing given; forwiernan takes a genitive thing denied.
models.accepted_alternatives: Withheld food from the stranger preserves the second meaning.
models.diagnosis: The English word food looks identical but the two Old English verbs govern it differently.

models.target: Dative governed by useful, subject-predicate agreement, lexical new noun.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: The goat is useful to the shepherd. Gāt is feminine nominative singular, the subject; scēaphierde is masculine dative singular, the person to whom it is useful; strong behēfu is feminine nominative singular agreeing with gāt.
models.accepted_alternatives: Of use to the shepherd is equivalent.
models.diagnosis: Behēfu agrees with the goat, not with the dative person; masculine behēfe would fail the selected agreement target.

models.target: Bounded seeming frame with a dative experiencer and neuter nominative subject.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: This seems good to me. Mē is the dative experiencer. Ðis is the neuter nominative singular subject and gōd the agreeing predicate; ðyncð is third singular.
models.accepted_alternatives: This appears good to me is equivalent.
models.diagnosis: The dative experiencer is not a nominative subject. This particular seeming pattern has an expressed neuter subject; it must not be described as syntactically subjectless.

models.target: Accusative experiencer in an impersonal hunger clause versus nominative personal adjective predicate.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Both mean He was hungry. Hine is accusative singular in the impersonal hunger construction, which uses third-singular hyngrede without a nominative person subject. Hē is nominative singular and controls wæs in the ordinary adjective predicate; hungrig agrees with hē.
models.accepted_alternatives: He felt hungry is acceptable for the first.
models.diagnosis: Do not change hyngrede to agree with an accusative experiencer as though that pronoun were the nominative subject.

models.target: Accompaniment and means expressed by the same preposition with dative.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: The monk came with the stranger. The monk fed the stranger with good food. Mid expresses accompaniment in the first and means in the second; it governs dative in both.
models.accepted_alternatives: By means of good food makes the second relation explicit.
models.diagnosis: Identical English with and identical prepositional case do not make the two relations identical.

models.target: Bare instrumental means, distinct adjective/determiner forms and noun syncretism.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: The monk fed the stranger with good food. The monk fed the stranger with that food. Gōde is the distinct masculine singular strong instrumental; ðȳ is the distinct instrumental determiner. The noun męte has the same surface used for dative/instrumental, so its ending alone does not distinguish them.
models.accepted_alternatives: That food is the required demonstrative meaning in the second; an article-like translation the food is contextually possible, but the teaching example selects that.
models.diagnosis: Do not call gōde a weak nominative merely because another paradigm cell has the same spelling.

models.target: Perception with a directly agreeing description of the object.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: I saw the stranger sick. Both ðone cuman and untrumne are masculine accusative singular. The adjective describes the perceived object and agrees with it.
models.accepted_alternatives: I saw that the stranger was sick conveys the meaning in English, provided the Old English analysis does not invent an expressed finite ðæt clause.
models.diagnosis: Untrumne does not describe the nominative speaker.

models.target: Substantival personal adjective versus an adjective modifying an expressed singular noun.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: The monk clothes the naked (people). The monk clothes the naked stranger. Nacodan is weak masculine accusative plural used substantivally in the first, but weak masculine accusative singular modifying cuman in the second. The articles and expressed noun/context distinguish reference although nacodan is syncretic.
models.accepted_alternatives: Covers/provides clothing for is defensible when the intended clothing sense is retained.
models.diagnosis: The ending -an alone does not establish number; do not supply a singular person in the first or a plural stranger in the second.

models.target: Independent dative person/genitive thing with denial.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Ðā munucas forwiernað ðǣm cuman mętes.
old_english_outputs: Ðā munucas forwiernað ðǣm cuman mętes.
models.accepted_alternatives: A grammatical order with the same dative person and genitive thing is acceptable.
models.diagnosis: Munucas is the nominative plural subject; cuman is dative singular, not the verb’s accusative object.

models.target: Independent dative person/genitive thing with granting.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Ic ann ðǣm cuman mętes.
models.accepted_alternatives: Accept source-supported first-singular spelling variants while retaining granting, dative person and genitive thing.
models.diagnosis: Granting here is not the ordinary sęllan construction with an accusative thing.

models.target: Nominal partitive with sum/hwilc, question structure and accompaniment.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Sume ðāra munuca cōmon mid ðǣm cuman. Hwilc ðāra munuca cōm?
old_english_outputs: Sume ðāra munuca cōmon mid ðǣm cuman.
models.accepted_alternatives: Reasonable word order variants are acceptable. The English question does not specify the number of the selected monks: plural Hwilce ðāra munuca cōmon? is also defensible within the assigned nominal-partitive construction. The displayed singular is one compliant model.
models.diagnosis: The first substantival head is plural. In the displayed question the head is singular; a plural head requires cōmon. The genitive whole does not itself control the finite verb.

models.target: Independent fela plus genitive plural.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Se scēaphierde hæfð fela scēapa.
models.accepted_alternatives: A grammatical order variant is acceptable. Manig with an agreeing noun can be valid language but misses the explicit fela target.
models.diagnosis: Fela requires the genitive scēapa in this frame.

models.target: Independent bare instrumental with strong adjective -e and plural present agreement.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Ðā munucas fēdað ðā cuman gōde męte.
old_english_outputs: Ðā munucas fēdað ðā cuman gōde męte.
models.accepted_alternatives: Mid gōdum męte is valid means language but does not meet the no-preposition target.
models.diagnosis: The food is masculine singular despite the plural participants; retain distinct instrumental gōde.

models.target: Independent distinct demonstrative instrumental and substantival plural adjective.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Ðȳ męte fēdde ic ðā untruman.
old_english_outputs: Ðȳ męte fēdde ic ðā untruman.
models.accepted_alternatives: Ðon is the admitted instrumental variant. Other grammatical ordering is acceptable.
models.diagnosis: The sick people are plural accusative; the initial means phrase does not change the first-singular verb.

models.target: Accusative plural experiencer with impersonal third-singular verb.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Hīe hyngrede.
models.accepted_alternatives: Hīe wǣron hungrige is a valid ordinary adjective clause, but it misses the requested impersonal verb.
models.diagnosis: Hīe is accusative plural here; the impersonal verb remains third singular.

models.target: Bounded past seeming frame with dative experiencer and neuter nominative subject.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Ūs ðūhte ðæt gōd.
models.accepted_alternatives: An order variant with the same dative experiencer, neuter subject and past seeming meaning is acceptable.
models.diagnosis: Ūs is dative plural; ðæt is the neuter singular subject, so ðūhte is singular. It is not a content-clause conjunction in this sentence.

models.prompt_original: Christ is the Son of God [God’s Son].
models.target: Genitive relationship and nominative predicate.
models.essential_meaning: Christ is the Son of God [God’s Son].
models.explanation: The bracketed target is God’s Son; sunu remains nominative.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Agreeing our and nominative lord.
models.essential_meaning: Christ is our Lord.
models.explanation: Ūre agrees with masculine singular dryhten; it is the possessive adjective.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Direct when question and perceived-object adjective.
models.essential_meaning: When saw I you (sing.) hungry?
models.explanation: The supplied context/model takes the addressee as male; feminine hungry is also defensible with a female referent.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Neuter predicate agreement.
models.essential_meaning: Gold is precious.
models.explanation: The lexical -e of dēorwierðe is retained; it is not a weak ending here.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.prompt_original: The Day of Judgment will come.
models.target: Genitive judgment-day expression and present with future reference.
models.essential_meaning: The Day of Judgment will come.
models.explanation: Dōmes precedes its head dæg, which has no separate article in the selected prior genitive target. The present cymð expresses the contextually future event; an automatic volitional willan translation is not required.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.prompt_original: The farmer says to the workman, I will sell this house.
models.model: Se ierðling sægð ðǣm wyrhtan: “ic cīepe ðis hūs.”
models.target: Dative speaking recipient; direct speech with future-reference present.
models.essential_meaning: The farmer says to the workman, I will sell this house.
models.explanation: The direct quote changes to first person. A separately justified volitional I will sell is possible if its infinitive is taught.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern. Where English will is interpreted as desire or willingness, permit willan with the independently taught plain infinitive. For the negative statement, a contextually justified refusal reading is valid. The present model is one future-reference route, not the mandatory rendering of every English will.

models.prompt_original: The workman answers the farmer, I will buy your house.
models.model: Se wyrhta andswarað ðǣm ierðlinge: “ic bycge ðīn hūs.”
models.target: Answering with dative recipient and direct speech.
models.essential_meaning: The workman answers the farmer, I will buy your house.
models.explanation: The farmer is the dative addressee; the house is accusative inside the quotation.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern. Where English will is interpreted as desire or willingness, permit willan with the independently taught plain infinitive. For the negative statement, a contextually justified refusal reading is valid. The present model is one future-reference route, not the mandatory rendering of every English will.

models.target: Weak comparative predicate and nominative comparison.
models.essential_meaning: Life is more than raiment.
models.explanation: Māre agrees with neuter līf; the new evaluation sense means greater in worth.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Locative on with dative.
models.essential_meaning: The stranger is in prison.
models.explanation: English in prison does not require a translated article.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.prompt_original: The merchant is in the inn.
models.model: Se mangere is on ðǣm giesthūse.
models.target: Locative neuter phrase.
models.essential_meaning: The merchant is in the inn.
models.explanation: Use dative giesthūse, not nominative giesthūs.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Clothe with accusative person.
models.essential_meaning: The father clothes the son.
models.explanation: Sunu accusative singular is endingless apart from lexical -u.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Feminine agreement.
models.essential_meaning: This world is great.
models.explanation: This follows woruld’s grammatical gender; the exact prior selected micel cell controls the predicate.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Feed with singular sheep object.
models.essential_meaning: The shepherd feeds the sheep (sing.).
models.explanation: The source explicitly specifies sheep singular; sheep’s unchanged spelling is not itself plural.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Masculine plural predicate agreement.
models.essential_meaning: The merchants are rich.
models.explanation: Welige is plural strong; presence of the noun phrase’s article does not make the predicate weak.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Drink with accusative beverage.
models.essential_meaning: The soldier drinks wine.
models.explanation: Wine is singular mass use.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Strong preterite plural with mass object.
models.essential_meaning: The monks drank water.
models.explanation: Druncon has the plural preterite stem, not singular dranc.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.prompt_original: The king sat on the throne.
models.model: Se cyning sæt on ðǣm setle.
models.target: Past sitting and locative dative.
models.essential_meaning: The king sat on the throne.
models.explanation: Setle is a seat/throne, neuter dative singular.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.target: Bounded on+accusative right-side expression.
models.essential_meaning: Stand on my right hand.
models.explanation: Number is not specified: selected singular stand, with plural standað acceptable. The source’s on his swīðran hand also occurs with static standað; this is a bounded idiom, not a universal rest/dative rule.
models.valid_alternatives_note: A defensible Old English alternative is not wrong merely for differing from the model; the stated case/number/construction target and meaning still govern.

models.prompt_original: All nations shall come to the judgment.
models.model: Ealla ðēoda cumað tō ðǣm dōme.
models.target: All nations and destination judgment.
models.essential_meaning: All nations shall come to the judgment.
models.explanation: Ealla agrees with feminine plural ðēoda. The source -e variant ealle is also valid if understood as feminine.

models.target: Reference and governed cases in connected discourse.

models.answer: Hine after the opening arrival is the stranger, accusative experiencer of hunger. Him after sealde is the stranger, dative recipient. Mē in the stranger’s quotation is the stranger, dative person denied. Ðē in the monk’s quotation is the stranger, accusative person fed.

models.target: Partitive and governed genitives; weak-noun syncretism.

models.answer: Ðāra munuca is a genitive plural whole dependent on nominative singular ān. Mętes is the genitive thing governed by forwiernst. Ðone cuman after geseah is accusative singular; the first cuma and later se cuma phrases are nominative singular subjects.

models.diagnosis: The selected genitive plural is munuca, not a spelling guessed from a different headword variant. Syncretic weak endings must be assigned from their actual clause function.

models.target: Recognize and productively restate bare instrument as a dative prepositional phrase.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Gōde is masculine singular strong instrumental, modifying męte in the bare means phrase. With mid: mid gōdum męte.
models.accepted_alternatives: The means relation is preserved; no other part of the reply needs rewriting.
models.diagnosis: Mid governs dative, so the adjective changes from instrumental -e to dative -um.

models.target: Independent complete connected translation.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: A certain stranger came to the inn. He was hungry, and he was sick. One of the monks saw the stranger. The monk gave him food and water. The stranger said, “You do not deny me food.” The monk said, “I feed you with good food.” The stranger ate the food and drank the water.
models.accepted_alternatives: Guest for stranger and lodging-house for inn are acceptable. The giving/feeding roles, quoted persons and sequence must remain clear.
models.diagnosis: Do not translate the accusative hunger experiencer as an object being made hungry, reverse the giver and recipient, or take mętes as the monk’s possession.

models.target: Supported source comprehension and clause structure.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: The Son of Man comes; all the angels accompany him in the first sentence’s elliptical coordination. All nations are gathered before him. He divides them into two groups, compared with a shepherd separating sheep from goats, and places sheep at his right and goats at his left.
models.accepted_alternatives: A future rendering is appropriate to the judgment setting; a consistent present rendering of the narrative forms is also defensible.
models.diagnosis: The nations are the nominative plural subject of the passive; the text does not express a separate agent for their gathering.

models.target: Source object cases, demonstrative syncretism and lexical gender.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Hīe is accusative plural, referring to the assembled nations as the object of tōscǣt. Ðā scēap is neuter accusative plural and ðā gǣt feminine accusative plural, the things placed by gelōgað. In the shepherd comparison scēap is also neuter accusative plural, while fram governs dative plural gātum.
models.accepted_alternatives: The exact source noun phrases may be quoted with their full verbs.
models.diagnosis: Unchanged scēap can be plural; gǣt is the umlauted plural and must not be flattened to the source’s singular gāt or inferred from English spelling.

models.target: Supported event sequence and comparison, without independent adverbial-clause production.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Each ðonne means then and advances the scene. Swā-swā introduces just as, comparing the division of the nations with a shepherd’s separation of sheep from goats. The ðonne occurrences are sequencing adverbs, whereas swā-swā introduces a finite comparison clause.
models.accepted_alternatives: As/just as are defensible English equivalents for the supplied comparison.
models.diagnosis: Do not invent a when...then subordinate correlation or read comparative ðonne than into these two occurrences.

models.target: Complete supported exact-source translation.
models.essential_meaning: Preserve the requested referents, case relations, number, tense and explicit construction target.
models.answer: Now the Son of Man will come in his majesty, and all the angels together with him to the great judgment. Then he will sit on the throne of his majesty, and all nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them into two groups, just as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. Then he will place the sheep on his right hand, and the goats on his left.
models.accepted_alternatives: A consistent present rendering is valid. Seat/throne and glory/majesty may vary defensibly. The angels’ coming and the final hand are understood; English can repeat them. The comparison describes the shepherd’s general action.
models.diagnosis: Do not make the nations the gathering agent, merge the two distinct nouns for majesty, omit the shepherd comparison, or extend the translation into the following royal speech.
